title: Interest on Reserve Balances
summary: The Interest on Reserve Balances (IORB) rate remained unchanged at 3.65% on April 23, 2026, holding flat from the prior day and the preceding several days.
key_points: Rate has been flat at 3.65% from April 19 through April 23, 2026
why_it_matters: IORB is the interest rate the Federal Reserve pays to depository institutions on reserve balances held at the Fed. As part of the current monetary policy implementation framework, IORB serves as a key floor for money market rates. The stable reading indicates no change in the Fed's policy rate setting or reserve supply conditions. This data point reflects the current stance of monetary policy and provides insight into short-term funding costs for banks.
market_structure_context: IORB is a critical component of the Fed's floor system for monetary policy implementation. It establishes the risk-free floor for short-term rates in the banking system. Banks with excess reserves earn IORB, which influences their willingness to lend excess reserves in the federal funds or repo markets.
